name: Pinkish Orange
lede: Pinkish Orange is a modifier name, an orange leaning pink; its one book appearance is a dictionary entry that links the phrase to the padparadscha sapphire.

sections.title: A plain description
sections.body: The name is plain grammar, pink plus orange, and has no history of its own [2]. It first appears in our sources in the xkcd color survey of 2010, and the ISCC-NBS system calls the swatch a vivid yellowish pink [2]. Its parent family is [[orange]], and near neighbors include [[salmon]] and [[coral]] [2].

sections.title: The lotus-colored sapphire
sections.body: Paterson's dictionary gives a useful anchor. Its entry for lotus-colour describes it as the pinkish-orange of padparadscha sapphires, padparadscha being the Sinhalese word for lotus-colour [1]. So the padparadscha sapphire is the one example of this hue that our books name [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive it appears in 0.04% of paintings (9), most often as an accent, as photographed [3]. It peaks in the 1500s, at 3.4 times the expected rate, and the earliest match is a painting of 1494 [3].
